title: IndicRecipeNutri
description:
A corpus of 219,386 Indian recipes across 378 source sites, with parsed ingredients in English/Roman, a 17-class allergen surface carrying an explicit unassessed sentinel, and estimated dish-level micronutrition; a typed knowledge graph of 222,539 nodes and 6,428,210 edges across 17 node types and 22 relation types; a 67-query retrieval benchmark with knowledge-graph-derived gold sets; and a synthetic collaborative interaction log. The food-composition layer uses the IFCT 42-nutrient schema but contains no IFCT and no Indian composition data; its values are USDA SR Legacy and UK CoFID.

Two-tier release. Structured, factual and derived fields are published under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 with per-recipe source attribution. Raw recipe prose is not redistributed; a rehydration index of source URLs and SHA-256 text digests is published instead, together with a re-fetch script.

Known defects are published, not hidden. An independent allergen and diet audit ships with the data. See the datasheet before use, and do not use the allergen flags for end-user safety decisions.

notes:
Corpus build v15; release version 0.7.1. The release is versioned separately from the corpus build — data/corpus/corpus_manifest.json records the pairing.

VERIFY YOUR COPY. Every published file has a SHA-256 digest in checksums/SHA256SUMS, and scripts/verify_release.py --strict-checksums checks the payload against it. A GitHub clone without git-lfs yields 130-byte pointer stubs rather than data; run 'git lfs pull'.

BENCHMARK RESULTS ARE NOT COMPARABLE ACROSS VERSIONS. The 67 questions are frozen, but their gold sets are re-derived from the knowledge graph on every release. Compare systems only within a single release, using the query and relevance hashes recorded in data/benchmark/BENCHMARK_MANIFEST.json.

THE ALLERGEN 'unknown' SENTINEL MEANS 'never assessed', NOT 'safe'. Do not flatten it to False. Read the allergen surface through scripts/allergen_surface.py, which keeps the sentinel intact.

ORCIDs are not supplied: an ORCID identifies a specific person and must not be guessed.
